stories.title: Consumer prices climbed 3.4 percent in August
stories.summary: Inflation stayed high from last year, fueling expectations the Fed will raise rates next week.

article.background: Inflation means the price of things you buy goes up over time. In August, overall costs rose 3.4% compared to a year earlier. Energy prices, especially gasoline, have climbed due to renewed fighting in the Middle East.
article.what_happened: A new report shows the cost of living in August was up 3.4% from a year ago. Rising gasoline prices were a main driver of that inflation last month. Investors now think this will push the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates when it meets next week.
article.why_it_matters: When energy and gas costs go up, prices rise for groceries, commuting, and other everyday expenses. Higher interest rates make loans more costly. That means car loans and mortgages could get more expensive for anyone planning to borrow money soon.

stories.title: August inflation report showed prices up 3.4 percent year over year
stories.summary: Prices rose 3.4 percent in August from a year ago, fueling debate about Federal Reserve policy.

article.background: Inflation measures how fast prices rise across the economy. The Labor Department tracks this monthly. When inflation is high, the Federal Reserve (the central bank that sets interest rates) often raises rates to try to slow price growth.
article.what_happened: The Labor Department reported Friday that consumer prices rose 3.4% in August compared to last year. That figure is fueling talk that the Federal Reserve may raise interest rates again. The goal would be to slow inflation further.
article.why_it_matters: Higher interest rates make borrowing more expensive for everyday purchases like cars and homes. They also affect savings accounts and credit card rates. The Fed is trying to balance bringing inflation down without slowing the economy too much.

stories.title: Federal court rejected Trump order keeping Michigan coal plant running
stories.summary: A federal court blocked a Trump order keeping a Michigan coal plant open.

article.background: Coal-fired power plants burn coal to make electricity. They close when utilities decide they are too old or expensive to run. Last year, the Trump administration ordered the Energy Department to keep a Michigan coal plant open past when it was supposed to close.
article.what_happened: A federal court ruled Friday that the Energy Department had no power to force the plant to stay open. The court said the administration exceeded its authority. The plant can now retire on its original schedule.
article.why_it_matters: This limits how much power the administration has to override utilities' closing plans for old plants. Courts can block orders that go beyond what the law allows. For most people, it means utilities will make more of these decisions without government override.

stories.title: Prosecutor leading investigation of Trump critics resigned
stories.summary: A special prosecutor brought in to investigate told the Associated Press he has left the role

article.background: President Donald Trump appointed an ally as a special prosecutor. This person was brought in to lead a Justice Department investigation. The inquiry looked into whether former law enforcement and intelligence officials acted improperly regarding Trump during his first term.
article.what_happened: The prosecutor told the Associated Press on Thursday that he has resigned. He left his post leading the investigation. The resignation creates uncertainty about the inquiry's future.
article.why_it_matters: For now, this changes nothing for most people. It shows how investigations into political figures can shift quickly. What happens to this inquiry next remains unclear.

stories.title: Philippines ferry fire death toll rose to 35 with dozens missing
stories.summary: Coast guard recovered 30 more bodies from the wreckage two days after the blaze near Coron.

article.background: A ferry called the MV June Aster caught fire in the Philippines on Wednesday. It was traveling from Manila to Coron, a tourist spot on Palawan island. More than 130 people were on board.
article.what_happened: The Philippine Coast Guard recovered 30 bodies from the wreck, bringing the death toll to 35. Forty-three people were rescued and received hospital care. More than 50 people remain unaccounted for. The coast guard could not board the boat until Friday due to toxic fumes. More bodies are believed to still be on the vessel.
article.why_it_matters: Ferry travel is common between the Philippines' islands. Accidents like this one show the risks people face when they use these boats to move between regions. Millions of Filipinos depend on ferries for everyday transportation.

stories.title: Houthis seized Red Sea island controlling entrance to major shipping lane
stories.summary: The capture threatens Saudi oil exports through the Bab al-Mandab strait at the sea's southern end.

article.background: Yemen is in civil war. Iran-backed Houthis fight the Saudi-backed government. Norm covered this conflict in September when the Houthis seized a port city. Now they control more territory along Yemen's western coast and the Bab al-Mandab Strait. This strait is a narrow sea passage at the Red Sea's southern end where ships pass to reach global trade routes.
article.what_happened: The Houthis seized an island at the strait's entrance. They extended their control over this crucial chokepoint for global shipping. The group recently resumed major fighting with the Saudi-backed government after earlier gains.
article.why_it_matters: Saudi Arabia exports a lot of oil through this strait. If the Houthis disrupt shipping there, oil prices could rise for consumers. Supply chains for stores and makers of goods depend on this route too. Instability here affects how much you pay at the pump and what goods cost in stores.

stories.title: Nearly 50,000 Yemeni civilians fled Houthi advance on Red Sea coast
stories.summary: Villages emptied as fighting grew near the strait connecting the Red Sea to the Indian Ocean

article.background: Yemen is the Middle East's poorest country. It has suffered repeated cycles of conflict for years. The Houthis are a military group that controls parts of western Yemen. The Bab al-Mandab strait is a narrow waterway near Yemen's coast. Ships carrying trade between Europe and Asia pass through it.
article.what_happened: Nearly 50,000 people fled a sudden Houthi advance in western Yemen. Entire villages emptied as fighting intensified. Families are trapped near the fighting with little food left. Aid workers confirmed the displacement and the dire supply situation.
article.why_it_matters: The Bab al-Mandab strait is one of the world's most important shipping routes. Fighting there disrupts global trade between Europe and Asia. Yemen's conflict could shift from a cycle of on-and-off fighting to permanent warfare. That would keep the strait unstable for years to come.

stories.title: Military aircraft blamed for UK air traffic control outage that grounded flights
stories.summary: Bad flight data from a military plane shut down the system and stranded hundreds of thousands.

article.background: The UK's National Air Traffic Services, or Nats, runs the air traffic control system that manages flights across the country. On Tuesday, this system shut down for four hours. The outage forced airlines to cancel more than 2,000 flights. Hundreds of thousands of passengers were affected.
article.what_happened: A UK military aircraft submitted faulty flight data into the Nats system, according to reporting by the Financial Times. Four people briefed on the incident said this bad data caused the shutdown. The system remained down for several hours before it was fixed.
article.why_it_matters: A single data error from one aircraft caused massive disruption across the entire country's air traffic. This shows how critical systems need safeguards to catch bad data before it spreads. The incident reveals a gap in how Nats protects against mistakes that can ground thousands of flights.

stories.title: Alexander Zverev defeated Karen Khachanov in straight sets to reach US Open final
stories.summary: The German won in three tiebreak sets to advance to his third consecutive grand slam final.

article.background: Alexander Zverev is a German tennis player competing in Grand Slam tournaments, the four biggest events in professional tennis. He reached the US Open semi-final to face Karen Khachanov, a Russian player and longtime rival.
article.what_happened: Zverev defeated Khachanov 6-3, 7-6 (7), 7-6 (6) on Arthur Ashe Stadium. The match lasted about 107 minutes. Khachanov pushed back in the second and third sets, forcing tie-breaks and saving set points, but Zverev held firm to win in straight sets.
article.why_it_matters: This victory sends Zverev to his third consecutive Grand Slam final. Reaching multiple Grand Slam finals is a major achievement in tennis, marking him as one of the sport's top players.

stories.title: Ben Shelton beat Frances Tiafoe to reach his first major final
stories.summary: Shelton won in four sets to advance to the US Open championship match on Sunday.

article.background: The US Open is one of four Grand Slam tennis tournaments, the sport's most prestigious events. Ben Shelton, an American, was playing Frances Tiafoe, also American, in the men's semi-final on September 11, 2026. Both players were seeking their first Grand Slam final appearance.
article.what_happened: Shelton defeated Tiafoe 4-6, 6-3, 6-3, 7-5 in four sets at Arthur Ashe Stadium. Shelton came back after losing the first set, taking three straight sets over the next three hours and 17 minutes. Shelton, ranked eighth, will now face top-seeded Alexander Zverev in Sunday's final.
article.why_it_matters: Shelton's victory makes him the first Black man to play in a US Open final since Arthur Ashe in 1972. For American tennis fans, this marks a rare moment when an American man reaches a Grand Slam final, something that has not happened since Andy Roddick won the US Open title.
